chunks: Al-‘Abbās ibn ‘Āmir narrated from Muthannā, who said:
I asked him about a man for whom a bequest was made, but he died before receiving it and left no offspring. He said: “Seek an heir or a mawlā for him, then give it to him.”

I said: “What if no guardian/heir is known for him?” He said: “Strive to find a guardian for him, and if you do not find one, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows your effort, then give it in charity.”

key_terms.فَتَصَدَّقْ بِهَا: then give it away as charity
key_terms.مَوْلًى: a mawlā, here a legally connected patron or entitled associate
key_terms.وَصِيَّةٍ: a bequest or testamentary gift assigned to a person
key_terms.وَلِيٌّ: a guardian or legally recognized responsible relative/authority
key_terms.يَقْبِضَهَا: to take possession of it or receive it

ai.seo_question: What should be done with a bequest if the beneficiary dies before receiving it and has no known heir?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a bequest owed to someone who dies before taking possession of it. The bequest should be given to his heir or mawlā if one can be found; if no rightful recipient is identified despite sincere effort, it is to be given in charity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5490 - Al-Abbas ibn Amir narrated from Muthanna who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a man for whom a bequest was made, but he died before receiving it and left no offspring.
Imam (as) said: "Seek an heir or his mawla (guardian) and give it to him."

I asked: "What if no heir is known?"
Imam (as) replied: "Exert yourself in searching for an heir for him, and if you cannot find one and Allah (swt), the Exalted, knows of your sincere effort, then give it in charity."
